a: used before a noun to refer to one person or thing, not a specific one
all: the whole of something; every one of a group
an: used before a noun beginning with a vowel sound, to refer to one person or thing, not a specific one
and: used to connect words or parts of a sentence
any: some, no matter which one; at all
are: plural and second-person singular of be
as: to the same degree; while; in the role of
at: used to say where something is, or when something happens
b: the second letter of the English alphabet
be: to exist; used to say what something is or how it is
but: used to introduce something that contrasts with what was said before
by: used to say who or what does something, or near something
c: the third letter of the English alphabet
ca: short for California, a state in the western United States
can: to be able to do something
cd: a disc used to store music or computer data (compact disc)
click: to press a computer mouse button
close: near in space or time; to shut something
co: short for company; used in business names
d: the fourth letter of the English alphabet
de: a word meaning of or from in French, German, and other languages
do: to perform an action or activity
e: the fifth letter of the English alphabet
ebay: an online marketplace where people buy and sell new and used goods
email: a system for sending messages electronically
en: a word meaning in or on in French and Spanish
et: Latin for and, used in the phrase et cetera (and so on)
f: the sixth letter of the English alphabet
for: intended to belong to or be used by someone; because of
free: not controlled or limited; costing nothing
from: indicating where something starts or comes from
function: the purpose or job of a person or thing
g: the seventh letter of the English alphabet
h: the eighth letter of the English alphabet
he: used to refer to a man or boy already mentioned
her: belonging to a woman or girl; used to refer to a woman as the object of a verb
his: belonging to a man or boy already mentioned
how: by what means; in what way
i: used by a speaker to refer to himself or herself
id: short for identification; a name or number that identifies a person or thing
in: inside a place, or during a period of time
info: short for information; facts about something
is: third-person singular of be; used to say what something is
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or idea already mentioned
its: belonging to a thing already mentioned
j: the tenth letter of the English alphabet
jul: short for July, the seventh month of the year
jun: short for June, the sixth month of the year
just: only; exactly; a very short time ago
k: the eleventh letter of the English alphabet
l: the twelfth letter of the English alphabet
la: a musical note; the sixth note of a scale
links: words or images on a web page that you click to go to another page
m: the thirteenth letter of the English alphabet
main: most important; the largest or central part of something
many: a large number of people or things
may: used to say that something is possible, or to ask permission
me: used to refer to the speaker as the object of a verb
microsoft: a large technology company known for the Windows operating system
most: the greatest amount or number; almost all
n: the fourteenth letter of the English alphabet
new: not existing before; recently made or discovered
no: used to give a negative answer; not any
not: used to make a word or sentence negative
o: the fifteenth letter of the English alphabet
of: expressing the relationship between a part and a whole, or possession
oh: used to express surprise, understanding, or pain
on: physically touching and supported by a surface; during a particular day
only: no more than; just one thing and nothing else
or: used to connect two or more possibilities
p: the sixteenth letter of the English alphabet
please: used to make a polite request
pm: used after a time to show it is between noon and midnight
point: a particular place, moment, or idea; a sharp end
points: plural of point; scores in a game
post: a message or article published on a website
q: the seventeenth letter of the English alphabet
r: the eighteenth letter of the English alphabet
re: about; concerning (used in subject lines and references)
rss: a web feed format that lets readers follow updates to a website
s: the nineteenth letter of the English alphabet; also used to form plurals and possessives
she: used to refer to a woman or girl already mentioned
should: used to say what is right, expected, or likely
some: an unspecified amount or number of something
state: the condition of a person or thing at a particular time
such: of the type already mentioned; so great
system: a set of connected things that work together
that: used to point to a specific thing already mentioned, or to introduce a clause
the: used before a noun to refer to a specific person or thing that is already known
them: used to refer to a group of people or things as the object of a verb
they: used to refer to a group of people or things already mentioned
this: used to point to a person or thing near you or just mentioned
to: in the direction of; towards a place, person, or result
u: the twenty-first letter of the English alphabet
us: used to refer to the speaker and other people as the object of a verb
v: the twenty-second letter of the English alphabet
w: the twenty-third letter of the English alphabet
was: past tense of be (he, she, or it)
we: used by a speaker to refer to himself or herself and other people
web: the internet; a network of connected pages online
well: in a good way; in good health
were: past tense of be (we, you, or they)
what: used to ask for information about something
when: at the time that something happens
who: used to ask which person, or to refer to a person
will: used to talk about the future, or to say someone is willing to do something
with: together with; having or using something
x: the twenty-fourth letter of the English alphabet; used to mean an unknown number or thing
y: the twenty-fifth letter of the English alphabet
years: plural of year; periods of 365 days
you: used to refer to the person or people being spoken to
z: the twenty-sixth and last letter of the English alphabet
